texts: bier, help others

Compose a doha showing that when the bier is lifted, the good done for others without hope of return alone accompanies the soul, so a person should spend his days helping others, not gathering for himself.
At the bier all that I gathered is left behind; only the good I did for others walks with me.
doha on helping others, since all that's left at the end is the bier
At my uncle's bier nobody mentioned his bank balance, only the countless favours he had done for strangers without ever asking anything.
doha on helping ppl without expecting anything back
Give your effort to others freely, asking no fee and keeping no account.
I spent my whole weekend helping a stranger move, and I did not even catch his name, but it was the best weekend I've had in a long time.

Please write a doha about how real goodness is helping another person with no thought of reward, thanks or recognition, and how such selfless acts are the only wealth that increases when it is given away.
do good, expect nothing
The arrow of ambition flies to its own mark, but the yogi's life is an arrow shot toward the good of all.
The yogi in our colony spends his day fetching medicines for the old and mending roofs for the poor, and says he has no time for his own liberation.
arrow, yogi, serve others
Write a doha about how a yogi who meditates for years but never lifts a finger for others is like an arrow never loosed, while service to the needy sends it to its mark.
doha on yogi who helps ppl being better than one who just meditates
doha on the ocean giving rain to the world without asking, like us helping others
ocean, giving freely

Compose a doha showing that the ocean sends its water up to become rain for fields it has never seen, and in the same way a good person works for the welfare of people he may never meet, expecting nothing.
My father worked like an ocean all his life, giving to everyone in the family and the neighbourhood and never asking for repayment.
The ocean gives itself to the sky that the fields may drink; such is the life that lives for others.

Write a doha about the leaf that shelters travellers at the crossroads from rain and heat, expecting no thanks, and how a person's life becomes holy when he serves anyone who comes along without asking whence they came.
doha on a leaf giving shade at the crossroads, serving strangers
leaf, crossroads, help others
At the crossroads outside our village an old woman gives water to every passerby from a small shed, and she has never once taken a coin.
The leaf bows to the wayfarer at the crossroads, shading all without asking who they are.
A life lived only for oneself is soon forgotten; a life given for others is remembered through the generations.
I'd like a doha about how a person who lives only for his own comfort leaves nothing behind, while one who spends his strength on others is remembered long after he is gone.
My teacher spent her entire life helping poor children learn for free, and years after her passing her students are still doing the same for others.
doha on living for others rather than just for yourself
live for others
A fisherman in our village repairs the nets of poor widows for nothing, and says it is the only prayer he knows.
doha on repairing nets for the poor, helping without payment
The net that mends for the poor catches blessings that the world itself cannot give.
net, free help
Please write a doha about the net-mender who patiently repairs the nets of those who cannot pay, teaching that to labour for another's livelihood without asking anything is the highest prayer.
The bell at the mosque rings five times, but our neighbour spends the hours between each call carrying groceries for old people, and I think that is also a kind of prayer.
mosque, bell, serve others

Compose a doha showing that a person can ring the bell and visit the mosque every day, but the real prayer is helping those in need between the calls, since service to others is worship that the Almighty never refuses.
The bell rings and the mosque fills, yet the best prayer is the hand that works unseen for others.
doha on mosque and bell, helping ppl is the real prayer

Please write a doha about how a person who does good for others without keeping a ledger of favours lives lightly and happily, while the one who counts every kindness he has done is always bitter and disappointed.
doha on helping without keeping score
My friend always reminds everyone of the favours she has done for them, and I decided to help people quietly without ever mentioning it.
The good that is counted is spent; the good that is forgotten is saved forever.
help without counting
I want a doha about the old man who applies his sacred forehead mark and then goes out to feed the hungry and carry the sick to the clinic, teaching that devotion shows in service, not outward marks.
My neighbour wears a bold forehead mark and spends every evening helping sick strangers reach the hospital, which is more than I can say for most devout people.
The mark on the brow is only a sign; the service of others is the sacred writing on the soul.
doha on a tilak person actually helping the community
tilak, selfless service
peacock, giving joy
The peacock dances for the rain-starved earth and asks no pay; so let me labour for others' joy.
doha on peacock dancing for others without payment
My neighbour's peacock-like grace shows each time she volunteers to cook for the whole building, and nobody ever thanks her but she glows.

Write a doha about the peacock who spreads his feathers in the rain to delight the village without asking for payment, and how a generous person works for others' joy and takes his own pleasure in theirs.
doha about a beggar who still helps others even though he has little
The poorest of the poor with an empty bowl may still share his smile; riches of service need no coins.
The beggar outside our station always helps the blind and the elderly across the road, even though he himself has nothing to eat.
beggar who serves
Compose a doha about the beggar who, with nothing in his bowl, still helps others cross the road and shares his last bread with a stray, proving that the habit of serving others needs no wealth.
I would like a doha about how the leaf falls to feed the soil, and the soil nourishes new growth, teaching that every ending serves a beginning and a good life gives itself to the world.
doha on a leaf falling to nourish others
The leaf gives its green to the season, then its brown to the soil; nothing in it is kept for itself.
When my grandmother's old garden shed a thousand leaves she gathered them for compost and said that is what we must do in life: give back.
leaf, giving back
doha on the forest giving everything to the world
The forest gives timber, fruit and shade, and asks nothing; this is the pattern of the noble life.
forest, selfless giving
We walked through the forest and I thought of how it gives us shade, fruit and medicine for free, and yet people go on cutting it.

Write a doha showing that the forest offers its fruit, shade and medicines to everyone, even those who come with axes, and a good person too gives his service to all without regard to who deserves it.
My friend works two jobs but still finds time to tutor neighbourhood kids for free in the evening, and says he feels richer for it.
doha on volunteering your time without pay
Compose a doha about how the best use of the time God gives us is to share it with those who need our knowledge, strength or company, since the hours spent in serving others are never lost.
give your time
Time spent on others is not spent but saved; it is stored in the hearts of those we help.
help the stranger
The one who lifts a stranger lifts himself, and no deed of service is ever small or lost.

Please write a doha showing that helping someone who has no claim on you, a stranger or a passing face, is the purest goodness, since there is no expectation of return and no weight of obligation to taint it.
doha on helping complete strangers
I paid for a stranger's medicine at the pharmacy last week and walked away before she could thank me, and felt happy all day.
Live giving all you have to the world and keeping nothing for yourself.
serve selflessly
doha on living selflessly

I want a doha that tells how a person who gives his time, skill and strength to others without asking for anything in return ends up the richest of all, because he has gathered the love of countless hearts.
Since I retired I have been teaching my neighbours' children for free, and I have never been so rich in affection.
serve before self
doha on putting other ppl first
He who serves another first has already won what matters most.
My mother always serves everyone at the table before she eats herself, and has done so for forty years without once complaining.

Please write a doha about how a person who puts the welfare of others ahead of his own comfort is the one who really lives, because the joy of helping fills him in a way that selfish pleasure never can.
Compose a doha about how the best of people never ask what they will gain from helping a neighbour, but simply see a need and meet it, and in doing so become the true benefactors of their community.
He saw a need and met it; no one asked his name, and no one needed to.
doha on those who just help without making a big deal
When the storm hit our area, a retired schoolteacher went around checking on families and quietly fixing small things, and never mentioned it afterwards.
quiet helpers
Compose a doha about the tortoise, which walks slowly but never stops, and about how a person's steady acts of kindness over many years help more people than a single grand gesture could ever do.
My grandmother carries the tortoise's patience in helping the neighbours' sick children every evening, slowly and without complaint, for thirty years now.
doha on tortoise-like slow steady kindness to others
tortoise, patient service
Slowly the tortoise walks, yet reaches all; so does patient service bless many lives.
I want a doha telling that a good deed done without hope of return comes back in unplanned ways, and those who serve the needy quietly will one day see their kindness blossom.
Do good in secret and forget it; the world will remember what you cannot.
secret good deeds
I put some money in a poor student's account anonymously years ago and recently learnt that he now treats the poor for free, and it moved me deeply.
doha on kindness coming back later in life
priest, selfless service
The priest who fasts and chants but serves no one is hollow; the one who serves is full of prayer.
doha on a priest who actually helps the villagers
Write a doha about the priest who leaves his chanting at the first cry of a neighbour in need and gives his time and strength to help, teaching that the finest rituals are acts of service.
Our village priest drops everything to carry sick people to the hospital, and I think he understands religion better than most.
In the temple of service the way is open to all, and the one who works for others needs no other altar.
temple, serve people
Outside the temple every Sunday a woman serves free meals to travellers, and I think her small kitchen is holier than the shrine behind her.
Compose a doha showing that a temple is only a building unless its devotees serve the needy, and that the person who feeds and helps others has made his own life a more sacred place than any shrine.
doha on temple vs actually serving ppl
water pot, heron, give freely
The village matron keeps a water pot outside for every passerby, and I once saw a heron drinking from it undisturbed.
doha on keeping a pot of water for passersby, heron too

Write a doha about a pot of water left at the roadside for strangers and animals alike, and the heron who comes to it, showing that giving freely without asking who drinks is the most beautiful kind of service.
The pot of water stands at the roadside for all, even the heron; thus a noble life stands for all.
doha on giving a cloth sheet to a stranger in the cold
On the coldest night of the year my father took the cloth sheet from his own bed to a homeless man shivering outside, and never mentioned it.
cloth sheet, helping stranger
Please write a doha about giving a cloth sheet to a shivering stranger on a cold night, expecting nothing in return, and how such an act warms the giver even more than the receiver.
The cloth sheet given to a shivering stranger warms the giver's soul more than the finest cloak.
To benefit another is to benefit oneself; the hands that give are always full.
do good to others
doha on how helping others helps u too

Compose a doha showing that those who spend their lives in service to others discover that service is its own reward, that giving brings more joy than receiving, and that a helpful life never feels empty.
Volunteering at the old age centre every weekend has done more for my mood than a year of therapy, and I'm grateful for it.
doha on helping a neighbour through a hard time
My neighbour's husband was in the hospital and I looked after her kids for two weeks, and I didn't even think twice about it.
I want a doha about how helping a neighbour in a hard hour without being asked is the most human duty of all, and how those who do it build a community in which no one feels alone.
help your neighbour
When trouble visits a neighbour, let your hands arrive before your words.

Write a doha about the heron who stands near the bell tower and, unlike the crowd, does not look for rewards, and about how true service is quiet, attentive and given freely like a patient watcher's care.
The heron stands at the bell tower's edge, asking nothing; the helper too keeps watch and wants no praise.
doha on bell and heron, service without wanting recognition
heron, bell, quiet service
The old gatekeeper who rings the bell at our school watches over the children like a heron and never asks for any credit.
The rope that lowers the bucket to draw water for strangers is the holiest rope of all.
rope, serving the thirsty
Please write a doha about the rope and bucket which draw water for the thirsty traveller day after day without complaint, teaching us that to serve without tiring is the highest kind of devotion.
doha on a rope and bucket giving water to travellers
My uncle spends every summer pulling the rope at the public pump, drawing water for the whole village, and he says it is his daily prayer.
cuckoo, give joy
A girl in our colony sings like a cuckoo at the community kitchen every evening and the tired workers eat with new energy.

Compose a doha about the cuckoo whose sweet voice delights everyone in the garden without asking for payment, showing that sharing one's gift with the world, whatever it may be, is the finest form of service.
doha on cuckoo giving joy to everyone
The cuckoo sings for all who pass, asking no coin; so too a gift shared is a gift doubled.
doha about a beggar who shares what little he has with other beggars
The man who begs outside our shrine split his only bread with another man who had nothing, and I felt humbled.

Please write a doha showing that the poor man who shares his meagre crust with one who has less is more generous than the rich man who gives a coin for show, because true service is measured by sacrifice.
The beggar's last crust, divided, outshines the rich man's chest of gifts, for it is given in love.
beggar sharing
My friend started a free library in his neighbourhood and refuses all donations, saying he just wants kids to read.
free service to all
Free is the service of one who gives, and no price can buy what it brings.
doha on sharing resources for free with the community

Could you write a doha about the generous person who opens his time, knowledge and belongings to the entire neighbourhood without asking a price, teaching that the best of lives are lived as a public gift?
Compose a doha about the heron who stands patiently at the edge of water in the moonlight, and about how the one who watches over others tirelessly through the night does so without need of praise.
The moon shines on the heron's watch; so does the servant's quiet vigil bless the sleeping world.
doha on heron and moon, a night watchman who serves everyone
heron, moon, silent watch
The night watchman in our colony stays awake under the moon for everyone's safety, never complaining, like a heron guarding the shore.
Write a doha about the grindstone that crushes grain to feed an entire village while asking nothing, teaching us that a life spent in humble work for others is a life of the greatest worth.
The grindstone turns for the hungry village; it asks no thanks and keeps no flour.
doha on a grindstone working for others without credit
My grandmother ground flour at the village grindstone every morning for twenty families and never took a coin for it.
grindstone, tireless service
The blind man with the forehead mark at our crossing hands out sweets to the children at festivals, and I am amazed at how he gives so freely despite his own lack.

Compose a doha about the blind man who wears the sacred mark and still finds ways to serve those around him, showing that giving does not depend on sight, wealth or strength but only on a willing heart.
tilak, blind man, serving
doha on a blind man with a tilak who helps others
Though the blind man cannot see, he serves; the mark on his brow is writ in deeds.
doha on the ocean giving to everyone, like a good person
The ocean gives its bounty and its rain to the whole coast, and my father gave the same way, freely to everyone who needed.
Please write a doha about the ocean that gives its bounty to the poor without once asking for payment, and about how a good life is an ocean of giving.
The ocean keeps nothing for itself; it rises to rain and falls to feed, a lesson of the noble heart.
ocean, generosity
doha on dew and needle, small acts of helping that add up

Write a doha about the dew that gently refreshes every blade of grass at dawn and the needle that quietly stitches what is torn, and show that small, patient acts of service quietly keep the whole world together.
dew, needle, small service
The dew refreshes the grass without a sound, the needle mends without applause; so do good souls serve.
My mother picks up a needle each night to mend the torn clothes of poor children, and each morning the dew is on the grass when they leave for school wearing them.

I'd like a doha about the elephant who carries heavy loads for the moneylender and for the village without complaint, and about how a person's strength is best used for lifting others' burdens instead of piling up his own.
doha on elephant carrying loads for others like a good person
Our moneylender's elephant carries the poor farmers' crops to town for free, and I think the animal teaches us what real strength is for.
elephant, moneylender, service
The elephant bears the moneylender's burdens and the farmer's alike; strength is a gift to be given.
doha on volunteers who clean up after floods

Please write a doha about the people who leave their own comforts to clean up after a disaster, feed the families affected and rebuild what was lost, and show that they are the living face of selfless service.
volunteers who serve
Hands that rebuild what the flood has taken are blessed; they need no name to be remembered.
After the floods our college students spent their holidays clearing mud and distributing food in the affected villages, and returned happier than from any trip.
The traveller who stops to help another on the road delays his own journey and hastens his salvation.
traveler helping travelers

Compose a doha about the traveler who pauses to help another struggling on the road, carrying his bundle or sharing his food, showing that a life of service travels farther than a life of mere pilgrimage.
doha on a traveller who helps another traveller
On my trip a fellow traveler gave me half his food and water when I ran out and refused to take any money, and I will never forget him.
stars, giving light
On a clear night the stars light the way for sleepless travellers, and I thought of my father who stayed up every night for years guiding lost villagers.
Compose a doha about the stars that shine at night for everyone without charging a price, teaching that a good person lights the path of others at the cost of his own rest and asks nothing.
The stars give light to the weary night and ask no wage; thus shines the soul that serves.
doha on stars giving light for free, like us helping others
Please write a doha about the owner of the inn who houses weary guests for free on winter nights, and the house of kindness he builds in their memory, which stays warm when all the beds are cold.
The old innkeeper at our village inn lets any stranded passenger sleep for free during the rain, and his house is always full of blessings.
The inn of the good keeps its beds for the weary, and the house of the generous never runs short.
house, inn, free shelter
doha on inn open for free for people in need
Compose a doha about the way a truly helpful person sees every other person as his own family, offering aid without checking caste, creed or status, because he knows all people are one in need.
After the earthquake, a young man in our town fed everyone who came to his place, rich or poor, familiar or stranger, and refused all thanks.
He asked not whose son you were; he saw your need and gave himself to meet it.
serve without distinction
doha on helping everybody equally

Compose a doha about the river that gives its water to fields and cities without a thought, and the philosopher's stone that changes everything it touches without keeping any wealth, showing the nature of true service.
doha on a river and the philosopher's stone, giving without pride
river, philosopher's stone, giving
Our river irrigates the whole district for nothing and my grandfather, who had a rare philosopher's stone pendant, gave out gifts the same way.
The river gives and the philosopher's stone transforms, asking nothing; so the noble life enriches without owning.
doha on the cloud giving rain without being asked, and a moneylender who doesn't
The cloud pours down on every field alike, while the moneylender counts what he has lent; learn from the cloud.
Please write a doha about the cloud that gives rain to every field without sending a bill, contrasted with the moneylender who counts every favour, and how a good person should give like the cloud.
cloud, moneylender, free giving
The village moneylender wrote down every favour he did while the old farmer who shared his water never wrote anything, and who do you think people loved more?
dew, sand, serving
doha about dew falling on sand, helping where it's hard
Compose a doha about how the dew falls gently on desert sand where nobody sees it and nobody thanks it, teaching that the best service is done in hard places and without any audience or applause.
My aunt works in a remote desert village where nothing grows but the sand shifts, and each morning the dew of her care helps the children survive.
The dew falls on barren sand, unseen; so does the servant of others give where none will thank.
The best of lives is a gift passed on; the best of hands are those that never close.

Could you write a doha showing that the purpose of strength, wealth or knowledge is to be used for the benefit of others, and that the one who holds them only for himself has wasted what he was given?
doha on using your talents to help others
I have a talent for fixing electrical things and I spend my Sundays repairing appliances for elderly neighbours who cannot afford a technician.
use gifts for others
My grandmother counted her prayer beads at dawn and tested her day at night on the touchstone of service: how many had I helped?
Write a doha about the person who turns prayer beads in the morning and then tests himself on the touchstone of service in the evening, knowing that devotion unproved by help to others is only noise.
doha on prayer beads and touchstone, service is the real test
prayer beads, service, touchstone
The beads count the Name, the touchstone counts the deed; true prayer is proved by service.
doha about a diamond and the sun, giving without taking
diamond, sun, giving
The sun gives light without a diamond's price; the diamond keeps its sparkle. Give like the sun.
Compose a doha showing that the sun gives light and warmth to all without being paid, while the diamond holds its sparkle for the few, and that a good person should choose to serve like the sun.
My grandfather, rich in diamonds, spent his last years working like the sun, quietly helping poor families rise each morning.
helping hands
After my surgery the neighbours took turns bringing meals, and I cried at how kind people can be when they see a need.
doha on neighbours who helped during my recovery
Please write a doha about the beauty of a community in which neighbours help each other through illness and hardship with no expectation of return, because such a community is a sanctuary for all.
Where hands reach out in love, no sorrow is too great, and no burden too heavy to be shared.
